headline: Election clarity sparks a relief rally, but AI-trade doubts persist
body: With the midterm result in hand — a Democratic sweep of Congress — futures turned decisively higher overnight, a textbook relief rally built on the removal of a known uncertainty rather than any shift in the underlying macro picture. Dow futures were indicated up roughly 1.5%, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq close behind, reversing a chunk of the chip-led correction that had dragged the Nasdaq 100 down over the prior sessions. The ten-year Treasury yield eased to around 4.9%, giving risk assets another tailwind. Earnings also helped differentiate within the AI trade: AMD jumped roughly 5% after hours on a beat, a contrast to the Amazon and Intel misses that had rattled the tape just days earlier, suggesting investors are starting to separate AI winners from spending-related disappointments rather than selling the group indiscriminately.

Underneath the relief, the mood is closer to cautious optimism than outright greed. The dollar slid to a one-month low on fresh worries about tighter AI regulation, an unusual pairing with an equity rally and a reminder that policy risk around the AI complex hasn't gone away just because the election did. Crude stayed choppy as Iran-related diplomacy continued in the background, a low-grade overhang rather than an active market driver today. Retail and social-media chatter produced no distinct signal worth citing, so this read leans on price action, yields, and the earnings calendar rather than forum sentiment. Net effect: a genuine bounce in risk appetite, but one resting on removed uncertainty and selective earnings strength rather than a broad resolution of the valuation and spending concerns that triggered the recent AI-stock wobble.
